cells.tense: Right now the exchange runs even between you and the people walking beside you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are owed and have stopped counting, and ask for it out loud today.
cells.core:
Things come back to you at about the rate they go out. You do not have to do the arithmetic. When something is off you feel it, say it, and it gets settled — no grudge kept warm, no scorecard under the table. Most people either give past their limit or stop giving to protect the count.

You do neither. You keep moving and keep the exchange honest at the same time, and because both are running, the thing up ahead stops being the only thing on the road. Staying here is quiet, not heroic — the checking stays light. Start auditing every trade in your head and the road shortens and the walking companions drift back. Let the fairness stay plain. There is one person you have gone silent with about something owed — say the words today.

cells.place: the road where the goal is still up ahead

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead the books are already settled in your head, and you are paying now for a return that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been carrying for someone, put it down for a day, and say nothing about it.
cells.core:
You are moving ahead of the actual trade. In your head this one comes out even at some point down the road, so you front what should be shared and call it being ahead of the game. The comfort has a hook in it: each kindness gets weighed against a return still out ahead. The weighing is what drains you, not the load.

People can feel the hook. They get the help and the expectation together, and they step back, which makes you push more. What this wants is holding without forcing — the kind that endures pressure and does not crush the other person with it. You do not have to make fairness arrive on your schedule. Let this burden stay with its owner. The road is still there in the morning.

cells.tense: You stand at a door you have already walked past, where the trade did not come out even.
cells.ask: Write down what you actually bring to one person, then send it to them without softening it.
cells.core:
You stopped expecting anything to come back, so you stopped offering much. It is not coldness — more a flat tiredness. You watch other people trade easily and it looks like a language you used to speak. The motion is still in you somewhere, but it has no direction, because the aim keeps sliding back to that door.

What is starved is not your drive. It is your ability to tell a real offer from an old reflex — to sort one from the other. That sorting is a practice, and it starts small: one person, one honest account of what you bring, no performing. Do it alone first if that is easier. The point is to get your own measure back before putting it in front of anybody.

cells.tense: You are already setting the terms of the exchange and calling it circumstance, or the other person's idea.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to the person across from you, that a fair thing between you was your doing.
cells.core:
You set the terms a while back. The deals you make, the way you split things, the small corrections you run when someone takes too much — that is your hand. Describing it, though, you leave yourself out, as if the situation arranged itself. The fairness is already running; your name is not on it. There is an act here — knowing what is true and holding it quietly before speaking it — and it is already yours.

The claim matters, because something no one owns can slip without anyone noticing, you included. One sentence to the right person puts the account in your name, where you can keep it honest.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is yours. You call it circumstance.

attempts.check: The record already gives me the door for Too Little — a room where saying it didn't go well — and for Too Much the forward tilt of fairness. The risk is that Drive (focused motion, not aggression) gets read as 'goal-chasing' and I write four cells about personal ambition rather than about how fairness travels between two people; the reader would reasonably say 'this is about my own pace, not about giving and getting.' A second risk: in Too Little I'm tempted to make the old room a wound with a cause, which the record doesn't say and the rules forbid. The asks survive being wrong because each is one visible act — make a list, put it in a message, offer one trade — that teaches something about exchange even if I've misread where it sits. The sentence that serves me more than the person would be any line where I sound like I know what the fairness cost.

attempts.check: The record supports fairness moving through exchange, seated in steady forward motion; it does not support knowledge of the person's history, their private account of themselves, or any universal about how things go for them. The one claim I cannot stand behind when I look again is the word 'everyone' in Too Much — a statement about all their transactions, where the card is about one capacity in one kind of moment; narrowing it to 'in this one' rather than the general case. My sentence that serves me more than them, if I am honest, is any clean aphorism about ownership in the shadow cell — the person gets a pleasing line and no place to stand. Everything below is narrowed rather than hedged, and a person who says 'that is not what is happening' still has one visible act and one way of looking.
